claim.why_it_matters: The printed ELEMENT column nests each phrase under its statement (and TERMINAL under INPUT, each ALSO under TRUE/FALSE or WHEN); the transcription flattens all rows to one level, so statements and their phrases are indistinguishable and the two 'ALSO phrase' rows lose the parent that distinguishes them. Neighbouring pages 740 and 742 keep the nesting with   indents.

verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of page 741 (XVII-33) shows a three-level indented ELEMENT column: statements flush left (DELETE, DISABLE, DISPLAY, DIVIDE, ENABLE, ENTER, EVALUATE), their phrases indented one level, and TERMINAL phrase (under INPUT, in both DISABLE and ENABLE) and both ALSO phrase rows (under TRUE/FALSE and under WHEN) indented a second level. The markdown for page 741 renders every ELEMENT cell flush with no   indents, so the hierarchy is lost: TERMINAL reads as a sibling of INPUT, and the two ALSO phrase rows lose the parent that tells them apart. Pages 740 and 742 in specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md encode the same hierarchy with   indents (and keep the dot leaders), which confirms that page 741 departs from the transcription's own convention. The level indicators and module columns on page 741 are transcribed correctly; only the nesting is missing. Because the nesting says which element a phrase row belongs to, this is a content (structural) loss and not only formatting. The table is in the informative difference summary, so it is not normative.
verdict.corrected_description: The claim is real but the kind is wrong: no content is misplaced. All rows are present, in the right order and with the right values. The ELEMENT column's indentation hierarchy is dropped across the whole page: the DELETE, DISABLE, DISPLAY, DIVIDE, ENABLE and EVALUATE subrows, the second-level TERMINAL phrase rows (under INPUT) and the ALSO phrase rows (under TRUE/FALSE and WHEN). Pages 740 and 742 keep that hierarchy as   indents. The transcription should restore one   per printed indent level. The defect is structural and sits in an informative annex table.
